- ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset: Provides tools for listing, reading, and creating/updating skills.
- EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset: Tools for querying and modifying Unreal Editor state: console variables, asset imaging,
actor and asset selection, viewport camera, content browser navigation, and Play-In-Editor
session control.
- EditorToolset.LogsToolset: Provides tools for reading the Unreal Engine output log and controlling
log category verbosity.
- WorldBLDToolset.WorldBLDToolset: Inspect WorldBLD editor session context: which product plugins are enabled,
whether WorldBLD edit mode is active, and landscapes / PCG volumes in the level.
Use EditorToolset.UEditorAppToolset for viewport capture and actor selection.
For WorldBLD / CityBLD / TwinBLD / RoadBLD packaging, cook, compile, or plugin-load errors,
call GetPackagingGuide before guessing.
- WorldBLDToolset.WorldBLDValidationToolset: Cross-product validation loop for WorldBLD agent workflows.
Aggregates City / Road / Twin issue finders into a shared FBLDIssueReport,
checks post-op readiness (rebuild in flight), and optionally frames evidence.

Typical flow after a mutating tool batch:
1. CheckPostOpReadiness (wait / rebuild if not ready)
2. RunValidationLoop
3. CaptureValidationEvidence on the top spatial issue if needed
4. Fix via product toolsets, then repeat
- CityBLDToolset.CityBLDToolset: Inspect CityBLD modular buildings and city blocks, list BuildingStyle assets,
assign a style, and regenerate a building. Does not open creator windows.
CityBLDDiscoveryToolset gives richer city context, preset descriptions, parcels and validation.
Mutating tools require a CityBLD license or active trial.

When authoring a modular BuildingMesh externally, use Unreal local +X for width, +Z for up, and +Y for the facade/front
(Blender -Y with this project's export convention). Use a lower-left back-plane origin. Keep the entire X/Z perimeter
sharp and perfectly rectangular: no beveled outer corners and no sill, frame, trim, or other detail outside the intended
X/Z bounds. Details may protrude only in facade depth (+Y). AModularBuildingActor spaces modules from imported mesh
bounds rather than intended geometry, so any X/Z overhang creates gaps. Verify outward normals, exact bounds, and two
edge-to-edge copies in Unreal after import.
- CityBLDToolset.CityBLDDiscoveryToolset: Understand a CityBLD city and the presets available to build one. Read-only: nothing here changes the level.
CityBLD concepts: a City Block (ACityBlock) is a closed outline, usually traced along road edges. Its District decides
how it is subdivided into Parcels and which Land Use each parcel gets. A Land Use spawns a modular building with one of
its Building Styles, a static prefab, or nothing. Modular buildings (AModularBuildingActor) can also be placed by hand.
Workflow: start with GetCityContext. Browse presets with ListPresets and read one with DescribeDistrict, DescribeLandUse
or DescribeBuildingStyle. Inspect the level with ListCityBlocks, DescribeBlock, ListParcels, ListModularBuildings and
DescribeBuilding. Run FindCityIssues before and after edits.
For CityBLD / WorldBLD packaging, cook, compile, or plugin-load errors (missing WorldBLD_Content, Unable to load plugin,
GeometryScripting), call WorldBLDToolset.UWorldBLDToolset.GetPackagingGuide — do not treat those as city-content issues.
Actor parameters take {"refPath": "..."} from these results; class parameters take ClassPath. World positions are
Unreal centimeters; fields ending in Meters are meters.

Modular-mesh authoring contract: in Unreal local space, +X is module width, +Z is up, and the facade/front faces +Y.
With the project's Blender-to-Unreal export convention, author the front toward Blender -Y. Put sills and other
front-only details on that side and verify the imported face normals point outward. Use a lower-left back-plane origin
(Min X = 0, Min Z = 0, back plane Y = 0). AModularBuildingActor advances modules from imported static-mesh bounds,
not from the intended wall geometry. Therefore the complete X/Z perimeter must remain a sharp, perfect rectangle:
never bevel/chamfer its outer corners or let a sill, frame, trim, or any other detail exceed the intended X/Z bounds.
Details may project only in depth toward +Y. After import, check the exact X/Z bounds and place two copies edge-to-edge;
they must tile with no gap.
- RoadBLDToolset.RoadBLDDiscoveryToolset: Discover RoadBLD road presets, style assets and the current road network (roads, lanes, junctions, endpoints).
Typical workflow: ListPresets -> DescribePreset -> (RoadBLDPresetToolset for new styles) -> RoadBLDAuthoringToolset
to place roads -> FindJunctionIssues (fix stubs with SetControlPoints, corners with CloseCorner) ->
RoadBLDBuildToolset.Rebuild -> FindGeometryIssues -> RoadBLDFeedbackToolset.CaptureViewport to check the result.
Two roads may only end at the same point if they continue straight. For a turn, draw one road through the corner
with a TurnRadius, or call CloseCorner.
If the user reports artifacts in existing roads (gaps, missing or distorted meshes, floating pieces), start with
RoadBLDBuildToolset.Rebuild bForceRebuildAll=true on that network before inspecting or editing anything.
For RoadBLD / WorldBLD packaging, cook, compile, or plugin-load errors (missing WorldBLD_Content, Unable to load plugin,
GeometryScripting), call WorldBLDToolset.UWorldBLDToolset.GetPackagingGuide — do not treat those as road-content issues.
Distances are Unreal centimeters; +X forward, +Y right, +Z up. Actor parameters take {"refPath": "..."}.
For style work, start from the RoadBLD reference kit: the RoadKit_USA sample presets under
/RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets (full list in RoadBLDPresetToolset's description) and ListStyleAssets entries
with bIsRecommended=true (sample sidewalks, crossings, lanes, modules, PCG graphs, master and sample materials).
- RoadBLDToolset.RoadBLDAuthoringToolset: Create and edit RoadBLD roads. Every call is one undoable editor transaction and fails atomically.
Junctions are not authored: they form automatically wherever roads overlap once the network is rebuilt. End a side
street exactly on the centerline of the road it joins (T junction), or carry it at least 15 m past that road's far
edge (crossing). Ends left inside, just beyond or just short of another road are snapped to its centerline and
reported in Warnings.
Two roads may only end at the same point if they continue straight; those ends are linked automatically. For a turn,
draw one road through the corner with a TurnRadius, or call CloseCorner. After Rebuild, run
RoadBLDDiscoveryToolset.FindJunctionIssues and FindGeometryIssues.
Edits are not visible until the network is rebuilt. Batch many edits with bRebuild=false, then call
RoadBLDBuildToolset.Rebuild once. Distances are cm; Z is elevation.
- RoadBLDToolset.RoadBLDPresetToolset: Create new road styles from JSON specs: road presets (lanes, markings, surfaces, modules, props, sidewalks) and
material variants of existing masters. Workflow: DescribePreset on the closest reference preset below to learn the
preset structure and the materials it uses, edit its Spec to match the prompt (set BasePreset, a new Name, and only
the fields that change), ValidatePreset, fix every error, then CreatePresetFromSpec and use the returned PresetId
with the authoring tools. For new looks, give material slots a Variant: {"Parent": master path,
"Scalars"/"Vectors"/"Textures": overrides} after checking parameter names with ListMaterialParameters.
Assets are written under /Game/RoadBLD_Generated.

RoadBLD reference kit (study with DescribePreset / ListMaterialParameters; reuse paths directly in specs):
Road presets (Preset Ids):
- /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/RP_Default_USA_Street_2Lane.RP_Default_USA_Street_2Lane_C (two-lane city street)
- /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/RP_Default_USA_Street_3Lane_1Way.RP_Default_USA_Street_3Lane_1Way_C (three-lane one-way street)
- /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/RP_Default_USA_Boulevard_4Lane_CenterTurns.RP_Default_USA_Boulevard_4Lane_CenterTurns_C (four-lane boulevard with center turn lanes)
- /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/RP_Default_USA_Freeway_2Lane.RP_Default_USA_Freeway_2Lane_C (two-lane freeway)
- /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/RP_Default_USA_Freeway_3Lane.RP_Default_USA_Freeway_3Lane_C (three-lane freeway)
Sidewalk presets: /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/Sidewalks/RSP_USA_StandardSidewalk,
  /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/RoadBLDSampleKit/Roads/RoadPresets/RSP_Sample_ConcreteSidewalk
Crossing styles: /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/Crossings/CP_USA_ParallelCrosswalk,
  /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/RoadBLDSampleKit/Roads/RoadPresets/CP_SampleCrossing
Lane presets: /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/Lanes/Lane_NormalDriving, Lane_BikeLane, Lane_Restricted (same folder)
Road modules: /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Presets/RoadModules/RM_USA_Curb, RM_USA_Gutter, RM_USA_Guardrail,
  RM_HighwaySupport, RM_HighwaySupport_Wide, RM_Photoreal_ProceduralBridgeBarrier (same folder);
  /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/RoadBLDSampleKit/Roads/RoadPresets/RM_Sample_Curb, RM_Sample_StreetLights,
  RM_Sample_Bridge, RM_Sample_ProceduralBridge, RM_Sample_HighwaySupport (same folder)
PCG graphs: /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/PCG/PCG_USA_CityStreet, /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/PCG/PCG_USA_Freeway
Master materials (Variant parents): /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/Materials/M_RoadBLD_Asphalt_Master,
  /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/Materials/M_RoadBLD_Sidewalk_Master, /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/Materials/M_LaneDecal_Master,
  /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/Materials/M_RoadBLD_EdgeDetail_Master, M_RoadBLD_Abutment_Master, M_RoadBLD_TireWear_Master
  (same folder), /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Materials/Kit_Freeway_A_Master
Sample material instances: /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/DefaultRoadKit/Materials/MI_RoadBLD_Asphalt_Road, MI_RoadBLD_Asphalt_Road_Worn,
  MI_RoadBLD_Default_Abutment (same folder); /RoadBLD/RoadBLD/RoadKit_USA/Materials/MI_USA_Sidewalk, MI_USA_Sidewalk_WS,
  MI_USA_Concrete_WS, MI_USA_Curb, MI_USA_Gutter, MI_HardnedTar, MI_RuralRoad_EdgeDetail (same folder)
ListStyleAssets flags all of these with bIsRecommended=true.
- RoadBLDToolset.RoadBLDBuildToolset: Build RoadBLD road networks. Rebuilding generates road meshes, junctions, markings, sidewalks, props and landscape
edits from authored roads. Rebuilds start on the next editor tick and finish in the background; with bWait=false
the call returns State=Running and a JobId immediately, so the job can be polled or cancelled.
When the user reports visual artifacts (gaps or seams, missing, stretched or distorted meshes, floating or misplaced
pieces, stale junctions or markings), first call Rebuild with bForceRebuildAll=true and bOnlyStale=false on the
affected network, then CaptureViewport to check. Change road shapes only if the artifact survives a forced rebuild.
Small scopes: call Rebuild with bWait=true. Large networks: a wait that exceeds TimeoutMs returns State=Running with
bTimedOut=true and a JobId; keep polling with WaitForRebuild or RebuildStatus instead of starting another rebuild.
- RoadBLDToolset.RoadBLDFeedbackToolset: Look at road networks. Captures frame a road, junction, network or area in the active level viewport, wait for
pending rebuilds, and return a PNG image so you can check lane layouts, markings, materials and junction shapes.
Captures require the editor UI. Keep images small (the defaults are fine) to save context.
When investigating reported artifacts (gaps, missing or distorted meshes, floating pieces), run
RoadBLDBuildToolset.Rebuild with bForceRebuildAll=true first; captures of a stale build are misleading.
- TwinBLDToolset.TwinBLDLocationToolset: Where on Earth the level is. Start every real-world replica here.
Workflow: GeocodePlace("Flatiron Building, New York") -> SuggestImportArea(place Location or Bounds) ->
SetGeoOrigin(SuggestedOrigin, bDryRun=false) -> TwinBLDSurveyToolset / TwinBLDImportToolset.
Geographic values are WGS84 decimal degrees ({"lat": 40.7411, "lon": -73.9897}); boxes are
{"south", "west", "north", "east"}. World values are Unreal centimeters, Z up. The geo origin is the real-world
location of world (0, 0); changing it after importing leaves existing content misplaced, so dry-run first.
Geocoding uses OpenStreetMap Nominatim (rate limited to one request per second, answers cached for 30 days);
search for specific places, never bulk-geocode lists.
For TwinBLD / WorldBLD / CityBLD / RoadBLD packaging, cook, compile, or plugin-load errors (missing WorldBLD_Content,
Unable to load plugin, GeometryScripting), call WorldBLDToolset.UWorldBLDToolset.GetPackagingGuide.
- TwinBLDToolset.TwinBLDSceneToolset: Inspect and fix content TwinBLD generated, with its real-world metadata.
TwinBLD tags generated actors TwinBLD.Type.<Type>, TwinBLD.Tile=<X>,<Y> and, for imports run through
TwinBLDImportToolset, TwinBLD.OSM=<way|relation|node>/<id>. Start with GetSceneContext, narrow down with
FindGenerated, read original OSM tags with DescribeGeneratedActor, then fix with SnapToLandscape, DetectFacades and
EditBuildingFromReality. Every edit is one undoable transaction. Actor parameters take {"refPath": "..."}.
Heights are meters in these tools; world positions are Unreal centimeters.
For TwinBLD packaging, cook, compile, or plugin-load errors, call WorldBLDToolset.UWorldBLDToolset.GetPackagingGuide.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.actor.ActorTools: Provides tools for inspecting and modifying actors, including
    their transforms, labels, parent-child relationships, and components.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools: Provides tools for interacting with assets in the Unreal project and files on disk.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.blueprint.BlueprintTools: Provides tools for working with Blueprints.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools: Provides tools for creating and editing CurveTable assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.data_asset.DataAssetTools: Provides tools for working with Data Assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools: Provides tools for creating and editing DataTable assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.material.MaterialTools: Provides tools for creating and editing Material and MaterialFunction assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.material_instance.MaterialInstanceTools: Provides tools for creating and modifying MaterialInstanceConstant assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools: Provides tools for inspecting and modifying the properties of
    Unreal Objects and Unreal Classes, including those in Blueprints.
    Also use this toolset to discover available classes and subclasses.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.primitive.PrimitiveTools: Provides tools for adding primitive geometry components to actors.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.scene.SceneTools: Provides tools for working with the currently loaded level, including
    loading levels, placing and removing actors, controlling the level camera,
    and organizing actors in the outliner.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.skeletal_mesh.SkeletalMeshTools: Provides tools for inspecting and modifying skeletal mesh assets, including
    the mesh/materials, bone hierarchies, and sockets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools: Provides tools for inspecting and modifying static mesh assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools: Provides tools for creating and editing StringTable assets.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.programmatic.ProgrammaticToolset: Batches calls to other registered tools through a small sandboxed Python
    script that glues them together with custom logic. The script's purpose is
    tool orchestration, not general Python execution.
- editor_toolset.toolsets.texture.TextureTools: Provides tools for working with Texture assets.

Geocoding uses OpenStreetMap Nominatim (rate limited to one request per second, answers cached for 30 days);
search for specific places, never bulk-geocode lists.
For TwinBLD / WorldBLD / CityBLD / RoadBLD packaging, cook, compile, or plugin-load errors (missing WorldBLD_Content,
Unable to load plugin, GeometryScripting), call WorldBLDToolset.UWorldBLDToolset.GetPackagingGuide.
- TwinBLDToolset.TwinBLDSceneToolset: Inspect and fix content TwinBLD generated, with its real-world metadata.
TwinBLD tags generated actors TwinBLD.Type.<Type>, TwinBLD.Tile=<X>,<Y> and, for imports run through
TwinBLDImportToolset, TwinBLD.OSM=<way|relation|node>/<id>. Start with GetSceneContext, narrow down with
FindGenerated, read original OSM tags with DescribeGeneratedActor, then fix with SnapToLandscape, DetectFacades and
EditBuildingFromReality. Every edit is one undoable transaction. Actor parameters take {"refPath": "..."}.
Heights are meters in these tools; world positions are Unreal centimeters.
